This `eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/max-params` is justified as a *temporary* deferral: the reason explicitly states that converting the positional signature to an object is "out of scope for this refactor." Per `LINTING.md`, `eslint-disable` should be reserved for *permanent* exceptions where the rule genuinely doesn't apply. Temporary/out-of-scope suppressions should widen the seatbelt baseline instead, so the violation stays visible and can still be fixed later. An `eslint-disable` here hides the extra parameter from the baseline entirely.

Prefer re-baselining with `SEATBELT_INCREASE` rather than an inline disable:

```bash
SEATBELT_INCREASE=@typescript-eslint/max-params npm run lint
```

Then remove the `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/max-params -- ...` comment and commit the resulting `eslint.seatbelt.tsv` diff.

The file-level `/* eslint-disable @typescript-eslint/naming-convention */` suppresses the rule for the entire file without an accompanying comment explaining why it is needed. A justification is required so reviewers and future maintainers understand the deliberate suppression, and a file-wide disable is broad enough to also hide unrelated future naming violations.

Add a short justification comment, e.g.:
```ts
/* eslint-disable @typescript-eslint/naming-convention */
// GitHub REST API request/response fields use snake_case (per_page, commit_sha, pull_number, etc.), which this rule would otherwise flag.
```
Better still, scope the disable to only the lines/objects that need it rather than the whole file.
